title: 冊府元龜 970, 外臣部・朝貢 — the Fulin king's embassy of Zhenguan 17 (643) and its gift of red and green glass
language_note: Literary Chinese, in the register prose of a Song imperial compendium built from Tang court records. The entry is not narrative and not description: it is a line in a tribute REGISTER, which is why it names a date, a ruler, an embassy and a list of goods and nothing else. 頗黎 is the Tang transcription for glass, not the later 玻璃.
date: Compiled 1013 CE; the entry records an embassy of the seventeenth year of the Zhenguan period, 643 CE. THE ERA NAME IS NOT IN THE EXCERPT — the text reads 十七年 and 貞觀 is established earlier in the juan. That boundary is stated rather than quietly resolved: the excerpt dates itself to a seventeenth year, and the identification of which is read from context this record did not capture.
original_text_excerpt: 十七年正月朔薛延陁百濟髙麗新羅吐谷渾康國女國閏六月墮和羅國十一月吐蕃薛延陁新羅婆羅門同娥西蕃處般啜等國各遣使獻方物是年拂菻王波多力遣使獻赤頗黎綠頗黎石綠金精等物陁洹國遣使來朝
original_text_note:
Verbatim Literary Chinese, 87 characters, COPIED BY HAND from Kanripo raw.githubusercontent.com/kanripo/KR3k0013/master/KR3k0013_970.txt on 2026-09-01, spanning the page boundary <pb:KR3k0013_WYG_970-11b> to <pb:KR3k0013_WYG_970-12a>.

EDITORIAL ACTS, DECLARED. Kanripo's ¶ line markers and its <pb:...> page markers are removed and the words they split are closed up. No punctuation is added; the source carries none.

WHY IT BEGINS AT 十七年 AND NOT AT 是年. The Fulin entry opens 是年, 'in that year', and the year itself is in the entry before it, across a page break. An excerpt starting at 是年 would have made a DATED embassy notice whose date was not in its own verbatim text — and the date is the whole reason this record is in the corpus. So the excerpt reaches back one entry to carry 十七年, and the record is self-dating to a seventeenth year even though the era name is not.

THE RECENSION IS THE WENYUANGE SIKU QUANSHU, and the page marker says so — the second record in this tranche whose own file confirms the warning F4_CANDIDATES wrote against Kanripo's base edition, rather than the warning being carried on the hunt document's authority. The orthography shows it: 髙 for 高, 陁 for 陀. The Qianlong editors are known to have altered passages about foreign peoples and this is a register of foreign embassies. No Zhonghua Shuju collation was performed because none is openly reachable from this project. Stated, uncollated, correctable by somebody opening a book.

WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ROME. A Byzantine embassy — 拂菻, Fulin — arrives at the Tang court in 643 and presents 赤頗黎 and 綠頗黎, red glass and green glass, with malachite and gold-essence. THIS CORPUS ALREADY HOLDS ROMAN AND BYZANTINE GLASS AS ARCHAEOLOGY, in eastasia-03-hwangnam-glass, in the Scandinavian records and in the Oc Eo material. This is the same substance arriving as diplomacy, named in a Chinese archival register, on a dated day. Object and text, in two records, about one thing — which is what the project instructions ask this corpus to be able to do and what no single record can do alone.

And the FORM is the argument. Fulin is one line among Xue Yantuo, Baekje, Goguryeo, Silla, Tuyuhun, Kangguo and the rest. Byzantium is not a marvel here; it is an entry in a tribute register, filed beside its neighbours. That is a different kind of evidence from the Da Qin descriptions in eastasia-01-weilue and eastasia-02-hou-hanshu, which are ethnography about a distant place, and it is the reason FINDING 45 called this the strongest East Asia candidate in either list.

THE ENGLISH SEARCH THAT FAILED, WHICH RULING 57 MAKES PART OF THE TIER. Named sources, not a count. Hirth 1885 — checked against the volume's own table of contents rather than against a bibliography, and the Cefu Yuangui is not in it. Hirth & Rockhill 1911. Legge 1888. Yule, Cathay and the Way Thither (1866). Four open sourcebook sites: Fordham's Internet East Asian History Sourcebook, Silk Road Seattle, silkroadfoundation.org, silk-road.com. Eight databases: archive.org full-text search, HathiTrust, Cambridge Core, ScienceDirect, DOAJ, eScholarship, academia.edu, ResearchGate, and Google Books. chinaknowledge.de's page for the text lists no translation.

THE BOUNDARY, STATED. Print-only monographs were not consulted, and one of them matters: Leslie & Gardiner, The Roman Empire in Chinese Sources (Rome, 1996), is the standard translation-corpus of exactly this material and nothing available to this project can establish whether it covers this entry. If it does, this record's tier is wrong and the correction is to name the page. That is the difference ruling 57 introduced: the claim is no longer 'no English translation exists', which no curator can establish, but 'this curator searched here and found none', which can be checked and, if wrong, corrected by naming the book.

FINDING 45 IS WHY THIS RECORD EXISTS AND FINDING 41 IS WHY IT ALMOST DID NOT. The nineteenth-century sinologists translated the dynastic histories and left the huiyao, the leishu and the geographies alone. The tier is fed by GENRE, not by obscurity, and genre is something a curator can aim at. This is the first record in the corpus curated by aiming at it.

NOT MEROITIC, and the distinction is FINDING 44's. Literary Chinese is a language machine translation can actually work in, so the tier turns the Part 6 path on and the path does real work. FINDING 44 recorded the opposite case — a text with better 'no English exists' evidence than this one, in a language nobody can translate, where the same tier would produce fluent nonsense attached to a resolving citation. This record is what the tier was designed for; the Hamadab stela is what it cannot see.

RULING 55, third and last. This is the third Literary Chinese record about Rome to enter the index in this tranche, and the one whose vocabulary — 拂菻, 大秦 by identification rather than by name — is furthest from the two china-describes-rome pairs. The prediction stays unread until the ranking check runs at the close.

subject_places.name: Fulin (拂菻)
subject_places.note: 拂菻, the Tang name for Byzantium, identified with 大秦 in the Xin Tangshu's own words (拂菻，古大秦也). Ground `regional` with no gazetteer id, as eastasia-01-weilue carries 大秦 and as record 34 carries it: a polity, not a settlement. It is the SOURCE of the embassy and the goods, which is what makes the Tang court the focus below.

subject_places.name: Chang'an, the Tang court
subject_places.note: The register is a record of embassies arriving at the Tang court, so the court is what every entry in it is directional relative to — the lesson ingest.verify taught this tranche on record 34, applied before the check had to say it again. Ground `regional` and no id: the entry names no city, and placing the court at a coordinate the text does not give would be resolving what the source left implicit.
